title: Intelligence + Continual Learning = Expertise — Yu Su, NeoCognition
talk_summary: Yu Su argues that raw model intelligence (reasoning over fresh context) is orthogonal to expertise (accumulated, situated competence), and that continual learning — adaptive compression of experience into reusable structures — is the bridge. He claims current agents are token-inefficient 'world's smartest novices' that brute-force every problem instead of compressing the search space with learned shortcuts.

takeaways.technique: Compress experience into reusable structures, not raw transcripts
takeaways.what_they_do: Defines continual learning as 'adaptive compression of the experience into reusable structures for future behavior' — vectors, graphs, skills, adapters, world models — rather than re-reading episode history each run.

takeaways.technique: Expertise compresses search space vs. intelligence expanding it
takeaways.what_they_do: Frames intelligence as brute-force search (spawn many parallel attempts) and expertise as learned shortcuts that prune the plausible solution paths before searching.

takeaways.technique: Expert pattern recognition over surface noise
takeaways.what_they_do: Notes experts looking at huge bug reports immediately locate the most plausible failure sites, and know preconditions/exceptions where rules bend — i.e., judgment and taste, including when to stop.
takeaways.evidence_quote: an expert is looking at like a gigantic bug reports they can immediately locate like the most plausible places where things could go wrong

takeaways.technique: Measure expertise per micro-world, not one global score
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues expertise is environment-specific and must be defined and measured per domain; the open question is how to define and measure expertise for any given environment.
takeaways.evidence_quote: how do you even measure uh define and measure expertise and this is probably environment specific

takeaways.technique: Bounded intelligence + accumulated expertise as a routing strategy
takeaways.what_they_do: Speculates that once raw intelligence crosses a threshold, better continual learning yields 'unbounded expertise from bounded intelligence' — so cheaper models plus strong learning may suffice.

takeaways.technique: Reliability vs. plasticity trade-off for agent configs
takeaways.what_they_do: Names the core tension: stable systems resist change, plastic systems embrace it, and asks how to reconcile — humans are the existence proof of both.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we want these agents to be both reliable and plastic, but they are inherently conflicting
